description:
Many environmental autosampler applications require accurate measurement of the liquid volume passed through each sample to properly characterize collected data. Conventional volumetric approaches, including timing-based methods and flowmeters, often suffer from limited accuracy, narrow flow rate ranges, high maintenance demands, or high costs. This work presents the TrueTip, a novel volumetric device utilizing a tipping bucket to address these issues. It is designed for in-situ filtration autosamplers, where sampled water must be expelled rather than stored. The TrueTip connects to autosampler outflow tubing, routing expelled water through a protective lid into the tipping mechanism. Bucket tips are detected by tipping bucket circuitry and conditioned by a debounce PCB, producing discrete pulses that are interpreted by autosampler control electronics as volumetric measurements. The hardware contains a field-deployable base, adjustable leveling mount, and circular bubble level to ensure consistent operation across varied terrain. Under specified test conditions, the TrueTip demonstrates an average volumetric error of 0.504%, supports flow rates from 0 to 800 mL/min, operates on soft or rocky terrain with inclines up to 15°, and safely ejects water under high-pressure conditions.
